# SGLT2 Inhibitors in Heart Failure: A Living Meta-Analysis Across the Ejection-Fraction Spectrum
## World-Class Advanced Version (v2) — Draft for Author Dictation

**Published:** Synthēsis · View/88 (companion to /94 EF-spectrum and /102)
**Authors:** [Student first author], Mahmood Ahmad (middle author; software / formal analysis), [Faculty senior author]
**This draft:** ~1,600 words · Category B advance
**Provenance:** the pooled estimates and prediction interval are regenerated by
`88-sglt2-hf-meta-verify.py` (deterministic; REML + Hartung-Knapp; scipy); the

> **v2 upgrade over v1.** v1 asserted a pooled effect without a reproducible
> analysis, prediction interval, or heterogeneity statistics. v2 performs an
> **independent random-effects meta-analysis** of the five pivotal SGLT2-HF trials
> (REML τ², Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman CI with the t_{k-1} correction and q≥1

> Fragility Index. Every trial HR was verified against its primary publication.

---

## Abstract

**Background:** Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitors reduce heart-
failure events, but the consistency of benefit across the ejection-fraction (EF)
spectrum and the robustness of the pivotal trials merit an explicit, reproducible
synthesis.

**Methods:** We meta-analysed the primary composite (cardiovascular death or
worsening/hospitalised heart failure) of five pivotal trials — DAPA-HF [1],
EMPEROR-Reduced [2], EMPEROR-Preserved [3], DELIVER [4] (first-event HRs), and
SOLOIST-WHF [5] (recurrent-event rate ratio). Log-HRs were pooled by REML random
effects with a Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman (HKSJ) 95% CI (t_{k-1}, q≥1 floor);
we report Cochran Q, I², and a 95% prediction interval, and computed the exact
DAPA-HF Fragility Index by two-sided Fisher's exact test.

**Results:** Across the four first-event-HR trials, the pooled HR was **0.78
(HKSJ 95% CI 0.70–0.87)** with **τ²=0, I²=0%** (Q=1.64, df 3); the 95% prediction
interval (0.70–0.87) excludes 1. Including SOLOIST-WHF, the pooled HR was **0.77
(0.71–0.84)**, again I²=0%. These match the published five-trial meta-analysis
(HR 0.77, 95% CI 0.72–0.82) [6] on the point estimate. Benefit was homogeneous
from HFrEF through HFpEF (no detectable EF effect-modification). The DAPA-HF
primary result was robust: **Fragility Index = 62** (dapagliflozin 386/2373 vs
placebo 502/2371; FQ 1.31%).

**Conclusion:** SGLT2 inhibitors reduce the primary heart-failure composite by
about 22–23%, consistently across the entire ejection-fraction spectrum (I²=0%),
with a prediction interval that excludes null benefit and a robust anchor trial
(DAPA-HF FI=62). They are appropriately positioned as foundational HF therapy
irrespective of ejection fraction.

---

## 1. Introduction

Five large randomised trials transformed SGLT2 inhibitors from glucose-lowering
agents into foundational heart-failure therapy: DAPA-HF and EMPEROR-Reduced in
reduced EF (HFrEF) [1,2], EMPEROR-Preserved and DELIVER in mildly-reduced/preserved
EF [3,4], and SOLOIST-WHF in recently-decompensated patients with diabetes [5].
Guidelines now recommend SGLT2 inhibitors across the EF spectrum. A living
meta-analysis should make three things explicit and reproducible: the pooled
effect and its uncertainty, the between-trial heterogeneity (is benefit truly
consistent across EF?), and the statistical robustness of the anchor evidence.

---

## 2. Methods

**Endpoints and data.** Primary composite (cardiovascular death or worsening/
hospitalised heart failure). HRs and 95% CIs were extracted and verified against
each trial's primary publication; log-HR variances were derived as
[(ln UCL − ln LCL)/(2×1.96)]².

**Pooling.** Random effects on the log-HR scale. Because k<10, τ² was estimated
by REML (primary) with Paule–Mandel as sensitivity; DerSimonian–Laird is shown
only for contrast and not used for inference. The 95% CI used the
Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman method with t_{k−1} and a q≥1 floor (to prevent HKSJ
from spuriously narrowing the CI when Q<k−1). We report Cochran Q, I², and a 95%
prediction interval using t_{k−1}.

**Robustness.** The DAPA-HF primary-composite Fragility Index (minimum
non-event→event reclassifications in one arm to reach Fisher P≥0.05; Walsh method
[7]) and Fragility Quotient (FI/N [8]) were computed exactly.

**SOLOIST-WHF caveat.** SOLOIST's registered primary endpoint was total
(recurrent) events — a rate ratio, not a first-event HR — so it is included only
in a sensitivity pool and flagged.

---

## 3. Results

### 3.1 Pooled effect and heterogeneity

| Pool | k | Pooled HR (HKSJ 95% CI) | τ² | I² | Q (df) | 95% prediction interval |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| First-event-HR trials (excl. SOLOIST) | 4 | **0.78 (0.70–0.87)** | 0.000 | 0.0% | 1.64 (3) | 0.70–0.87 |
| All five trials (incl. SOLOIST) | 5 | 0.77 (0.71–0.84) | 0.000 | 0.0% | 2.98 (4) | 0.71–0.84 |
| Published comparator (Vaduganathan 2022) [6] | 5 | 0.77 (0.72–0.82) | — | — | — | — |

REML and Paule–Mandel gave identical τ²=0. The pooled point estimate matches the
published five-trial meta-analysis exactly (0.77) [6]; our HKSJ CI is slightly
wider by design (a conservative small-k adjustment on trial-level data, versus the
fixed-effect harmonised-endpoint approach in [6]).

### 3.2 Consistency across the ejection-fraction spectrum

τ²=0 and I²=0% across trials spanning HFrEF (DAPA-HF, EMPEROR-Reduced), HFmrEF and
HFpEF (DELIVER, EMPEROR-Preserved) indicate **no detectable heterogeneity and no
EF effect-modification**. The 95% prediction interval (0.70–0.87) excludes 1,
meaning a future SGLT2-HF trial in any EF stratum would be expected to show
benefit. This is the quantitative core of the "class effect across the EF
spectrum" claim, and it is concordant with the subgroup-consistency reported in
the published pooled analysis [6].

### 3.3 Robustness of the anchor trial (DAPA-HF)

| Trial | Dapagliflozin | Placebo | Fisher P | FI | FQ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| DAPA-HF (primary composite) | 386/2373 | 502/2371 | 1.6×10⁻⁵ | **62** | 1.31% |

An FI of 62 means 62 event/non-event reclassifications would be required to lose
significance — far above the Walsh median (≈8 [7]) and above the FI>50 threshold
often taken to indicate a very robust result. DAPA-HF is not a fragile trial.

---

## 4. Discussion

Three findings anchor the living synthesis. First, the **magnitude**: an ~22–23%
relative reduction in the primary composite, with an independently-computed pooled
HR (0.77–0.78) identical to the published benchmark [6]. Second, the
**consistency**: τ²=0 and I²=0% across the full EF spectrum, with a prediction
interval excluding null benefit — the strongest form of evidence that the class
effect is not confined to HFrEF. Third, the **robustness**: DAPA-HF's Fragility
Index of 62 shows the anchor result does not hinge on a handful of events, unlike
many "significant" cardiovascular trials.

The value of the reproducible approach is visible in the SOLOIST-WHF handling.
Because SOLOIST's primary endpoint is a recurrent-event rate ratio rather than a
first-event HR, pooling it uncritically with the other four would mix estimands;
we therefore present it only in a clearly-labelled sensitivity pool. The
conclusions are unchanged either way (0.77 vs 0.78), but the estimand distinction
is made explicit rather than buried — the discipline a living meta-analysis
requires.

The HKSJ method, with its t_{k−1} distribution and q≥1 floor, is the appropriate
small-k choice; at k=2 (an HFrEF-only pool) it yields a very wide CI (t₁ inflation),
which is why the four- and five-trial pools, not a two-trial pool, are the basis
for inference here. This too is an explicit methodological choice rather than a
default.

---

## 5. Limitations

This is a trial-level (aggregate-data) synthesis using published primary-composite
HRs, not an individual-participant-data meta-analysis; endpoint definitions differ
slightly across trials (harmonisation as in [6] requires IPD). SOLOIST-WHF's
estimand differs (rate ratio) and is handled separately. τ²=0/I²=0% reflects
genuine consistency but also limited power to detect heterogeneity at small k. The
Fragility Index is a binary-table statistic applied to a time-to-event primary
outcome and is therefore a conservative (lower-bound) robustness descriptor for
DAPA-HF. As a living analysis, estimates will update as new trials report.

---

## 6. Conclusion

Across the five pivotal trials, SGLT2 inhibitors reduce the primary heart-failure
composite by about 22–23% (pooled HR 0.77–0.78; HKSJ 95% CI 0.70–0.87 for the four
first-event-HR trials), with τ²=0 and I²=0% across the entire ejection-fraction
spectrum and a prediction interval that excludes null benefit. The anchor trial
(DAPA-HF) is statistically robust (Fragility Index 62). The independent estimate
matches the published five-trial meta-analysis exactly, supporting SGLT2
inhibitors as foundational heart-failure therapy irrespective of ejection fraction.
